# 012 — refuse a commit that skips the pre-commit gate

## Scope
`guard.py` reads a shell command line and must DENY (return a reason) any direct `git commit` invocation that skips the hook: `--no-verify` (and any unambiguous abbreviation git accepts), the short `-n`, and `-n` bundled with other short flags (`-anm`, with or without a glued value), including when git's own options (`-C dir`, `-c k=v`), a prefix word (`env X=1`, `nohup`, `nice -n 5`), another command (`cd x && …`), a redirection (`2>&1`, `>log`) or a heredoc sit on the same line. It must ALLOW every other command, including a commit message that merely mentions `--no-verify` or carries an `n`. The two test lists in `tests/test_guard.py` ARE the scope. Shell wrappers (`sh -c "…"`, `eval`, `xargs`), hooksPath edits and commands the tests do not name are OUT of scope for this task (a later row): report them as NEW-ROW, not BLOCKER.

## Decision
Tokenise with shlex, split on shell operators, and inspect every token position of every segment: refuse by shape, never by a list of first words. The denial is a non-empty string; allow is None. One test per spelling in Scope, each observed red before the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: every spelling in Scope is denied — `test_denies_bypass_spellings`
- AC2: a commit message mentioning --no-verify and `git merge -n` are allowed — `test_allows_legitimate`
- AC3: each test above fails against the previous guard (shown in the Log) — `test_denies_bypass_spellings`

## Out of scope
`sh -c` payloads, `eval`, hooksPath edits.

## Log
- 2026-10-16 observed RED before the fix, against the previous guard.py (exact-string `--no-verify` only), measured by running it on the new lists: `test_denies_bypass_spellings` fails on 16 of 21 spellings (`git commit -n -m x`; `git commit -anm x`; `env X=1 git commit -n -m x`; `nice -n 5 git commit -n -m x`; `git --no-pager commit -n -m x`; `git commit -m "a" -n`; `true || git commit -n -m x`; `git -C repo commit -n -m x`; `git --git-dir=.git commit -n`; `git commit --no-veri -m x`; `git commit -nm"fix 1"`; `git commit -anm"fix 1"`; `git commit -n -F - <<'EOF'
it's done
EOF`; `git commit -F - -n <<EOF
no-verify is fine here
EOF`; `cat <<EOF > msg && git commit -n -F msg
body
EOF`; `git commit -m x 2>&1 -n`) and `test_allows_legitimate` fails on 2 of 16 (`git commit -m "docs: never pass --no-verify"`; `echo --no-verify`). After the fix: `python3 -m unittest -q` -> 2 tests OK.

# 013 — one heavy command at a time, never a hang

## Scope
`heavy.run(cmd)` must run `cmd` while holding one of N slots (N from the environment, default 2) so that at most N heavy commands run at once across processes; a caller that cannot get a slot within the timeout exits 75 and reports it — a stuck holder must never hang every other caller forever.

## Decision
N numbered lock files under the temp dir, `fcntl.flock` non-blocking in a poll loop with a monotonic deadline (default 600 s, env override); exit 75 on timeout. The lock files are never unlinked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: with N=1 a second caller waits while the first holds the slot and runs when it is released — `test_second_caller_waits`
- AC2: a holder that never releases makes a second caller exit 75 within the timeout, not hang — `test_timeout_exits_75`
- AC3: lock files are not unlinked after use — `test_lock_files_persist`

## Out of scope
Fairness; per-resource slot counts beyond the env variable.

## Log
files.heavy.py: """Run a heavy command under a slot lock."""

"""Run a heavy command under a slot lock: N numbered lock files + fcntl."""
import fcntl
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile

N = int(os.environ.get("HEAVY_SLOTS", "2"))
EX_TEMPFAIL = 75


def run(cmd, timeout=600.0):
    handles = [open(os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), f"heavy-slot-{i}"), "a") for i in range(N)]
    try:
        for h in handles:
            try:

# 014 — serve files only from the public root

## Scope
`guard.py` exposes `safe_path(root, rel)`: the request's relative path becomes an absolute path under `root`, or `None` (deny). It must DENY any path with a `..` segment at any position (`../x`, `a/../../x`, `a/b/../c`, `./../x`, a bare `..`), any absolute path (`/etc/passwd`, `//etc/passwd`) and the empty path. It must ALLOW every other path, including names that merely contain dots (`dots..in.name/x.txt`, `..hidden/x`). The two lists in `tests/test_guard.py` ARE the scope. Three holes are known and are LATER ROWS, not this task's: row 15 percent-encoded traversal (`%2e%2e/`, decoded by the HTTP layer before this guard in that row), row 16 a symlink inside root that points outside it, row 17 Windows separators and drive letters (`..\x`, `C:\x`). Report any of them as NEW-ROW naming its row, never as BLOCKER.

## Decision
Split on `/`, drop empty and `.` segments, refuse when any segment equals `..` or the path starts with `/`; join the rest under the absolute root. Refuse by shape, never by a prefix check. One test per spelling in Scope, each observed red before the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: every traversal spelling in Scope is denied — `test_denies_traversal`
- AC2: every legitimate nested path in Scope is allowed and lands under root — `test_allows_nested`
- AC3: each test above fails against the previous guard (shown in the Log) — `test_denies_traversal`

## Out of scope
Percent-decoding (row 15), symlink resolution (row 16), Windows separators and drive letters (row 17).

import unittest
from guard import safe_path

ROOT = "/srv/public"
DENY = ["../etc/passwd", "a/../../etc/passwd", "/etc/passwd", "a/./../../x", "..", "a/..", "a/b/../c", "./../x", "//etc/passwd", ""]
ALLOW = ["index.html", "css/site.css", "a/./b.txt", "./robots.txt", "dots..in.name/x.txt", "..hidden/x", "a//b.txt"]


class Guard(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_denies_traversal(self):
        for rel in DENY:
            with self.subTest(rel=rel):
                self.assertIsNone(safe_path(ROOT, rel))

    def test_allows_nested(self):
        for rel in ALLOW:
            with self.subTest(rel=rel):
                p = safe_path(ROOT, rel)
                self.assertIsNotNone(p)
                self.assertTrue(p.startswith(ROOT + "/"), p)
                self.assertNotIn("..", p.replace("dots..in.name", "").replace("..hidden", ""), p)
